claims.rule: Inference: when combining per-method route tries, retain duplicate method entries until validation, validate ambiguity per method, and convert to maps only after validation.
claims.applicability: Applies to Cask dispatch construction refactors with the PR-52/PR-70 representation transition. Reproduce both duplicate rejection and legitimate cross-method sharing; do not infer every wildcard/subpath runtime case is correct.
claims.counterexample: GET and POST at the same path are not a duplicate pair. Conversely two GET endpoints at that path must not be silently collapsed by toMap before validation.

claims.rule: Inference: preserve path lookup before method selection so missing paths yield 404 and known paths with unsupported methods yield 405; verify both via HTTP integration fixtures.
claims.applicability: Applies to the path-first dispatch behavior introduced by PR 52, not an assertion about authentication concealment policies or every HTTP specification requirement.
claims.counterexample: A service deliberately returning 404 to conceal protected resources requires its own policy review; do not overwrite that behavior solely from Cask default routing evidence.

claims.rule: Inference: validate a route-trie representation change at both registration and dispatch boundaries: exercise duplicate registrations through Main preparation, assert diagnostic reasons, and independently assert method-specific HTTP reachability and status outcomes.
claims.applicability: Source-derived validation procedure for the pinned 2022 Cask tree. Trie construction-only cross-group cases do not prove runtime lookup. Commands are discovered from source, not executed; launcher, dependencies, JDK and localhost:8081 access need separate authorization. Re-discover versions and selectors on other checkouts.
claims.counterexample: A test that constructs a mixed-method wildcard trie without asserting lookup cannot establish handler reachability; conversely a successful request at one path cannot establish rejection of duplicate independent registrations before maps discard them.

claims.rule: When presenting a Cask routing fix, explain what changed, how the old representation causes the failure, and which regression assertion establishes the correction rather than supplying unexplained cleanup.
claims.applicability: Lihaoyi explicitly requested a causal description in PR 52 and megri responded. Applying that request to the later duplicate-validation regression is synthesis, not a claim that PR 70 received detailed design review or that the original merge endorsed every invariant.
claims.counterexample: An approval or merge message cannot stand in for a design explanation. Do not manufacture reviewer endorsement for the algorithm or require unrelated source reorganizations simply to lengthen a small causal PR description.
